plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do. This holds because your payment depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than your value, and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since all bidders are rational and know this, they will also bid their true values. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $34 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the price you'd pay, and never pay more than your value. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since this holds regardless of competitors' strategies, I should bid exactly my private value of $28.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays the second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other rational bidders do—overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since my value is $14, bidding exactly $14 maximizes my expected profit regardless of others' beliefs or strategies.
